events.details: Please join us for a book launch of That Directionless Light of the Future: Rediscovering Russell FitzGerald with editor Jon Davies. Stop by to pick up a copy of the publication and enjoy refreshments and a drop-in signing with the editor. Join us for brief remarks at 6pm. That Directionless Light of the Future: Rediscovering Russell FitzGerald is the first major publication devoted to artist Russell FitzGerald. Bringing together newly commissioned scholarship and more than 90 reproductions of paintings, drawings, illustrations, archival material the book offers the first comprehensive account of an artist whose ambitious vision has remained hidden for decades. Edited by Canadian art historian and curator Jon Davies, this handsome volume brings together reproductions of the artist’s work and other material with new texts by Davies, Dodie Bellamy, and Jamie Parra to return FitzGerald to art history and consider his relevance to the present. events.details: From November 21 to December 3, join the 7th Mulan International Film Festival at Toronto’s Innis Town Hall. As the largest film festival dedicated to Chinese-language cinema in North America, Mulan brings restored classics and new voices to the big screen. Opening night presents the Canadian premiere of the 4K restoration of Patrick TAM’s Love Massacre, starring Brigitte LIN. The festival closes with the North American premiere of CHONG Keat Aun’s Golden Horse Award-winning Mother Bhumi, winner of Best Leading Actress for FAN Bingbing, Best Cinematography and Best Original Film Song. Discover six features and nine shorts from emerging filmmakers in the Fountainhead competition programme, and vote for your favourites. Other highlights include the world premiere of the new 4K restoration of Clara LAW’s Farewell, China, starring Maggie CHEUNG and Tony LEUNG Ka-Fai, and On Canvas, On Stage, a complete retrospective of QIU Jiongjiong’s films, including A New Old Play and Madame. events.details: You know that part of a house party when everyone somehow ends up in the kitchen while a few people are dancing their hearts out in the living room? Someone’s pouring another drink, someone’s telling a story with way too much detail, and you’re pretending you came back for a little snack when really you wanted to keep talking to that cute person you just met! That’s the feeling we want you to have at Come Over. A night where you can show up with your friends, make a few new ones, and go from deep conversation to dancing in the time it takes for the DJ to play your song. Stay for a drink, stay for a dance, stay because you said goodbye twenty minutes ago and somehow you’re still here. And yes, babe, there’s food. Every edition, Proud Palate will put out a beautiful grazing board for everyone to snack on throughout the night. Have a little bite when you get in, go back for more between songs, and use “I’m just grabbing something to eat” as an excuse to walk past your crush one more time. We get it. The Experience For the first two hours of every Come Over, there’s a little extra you can opt into.

venue.address: 50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4

events.description: “There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”
events.details: “There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.” This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession. In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop. Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us. Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th Get your tickets today https://soulpepper.ca/whats-on/de-profundis-oscar-wilde-in-jail/ !

events.details: Emma Lamontagne has reintroduced herself with her new EP title “Inevitable,” a 5-song collection of her life before turning 25. The EP has landed her an Ontario Folk Music Award nomination for Song of the Year, as well as a Capital Music Award nomination for Songwriter of the Year. Her emotionally riveting voice has received praise from fans who have described her songwriting and stand-up comedy as if she is watching their lives through a camera lens. She has shared the stage with Donovan Woods, Tyler Shaw, Forest Blakk, Elijah Woods, TALK and many more. Emma is currently deep in the midst of writing her long-awaited sophomore album, which will be a dark, soulful detailing of her feminine experience as she moves through her quarter-life crisis. Instagram YouTube Website Spotify With special guest Meagan De Lima Meagan De Lima is a Toronto singer-songwriter crafting sweet & soulful R&B from the heart. Her goal is to make her listeners feel seen and heard through her music. Meagan’s grandfathers were both jazz musicians who performed in India (Goa), Africa (Nairobi), and Canada (Toronto) when they immigrated in the 60s. This motivated her to follow her dreams and create music.

events.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming shoe museum. Located in Toronto, Canada, the Bata Shoe Museum regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artifacts, chosen from a collection of nearly 15,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. Over 4,500 years of history are reflected in our permanent exhibition, All About Shoes while our three other galleries feature changing exhibitions – so there’s always something new to see.

events.details: Exit Points is a live music series that invites you into the world of musical improvisation, even if it’s your first time. Each event begins with simple listening strategies to help you feel more at ease with unfamiliar sounds and forms. You’ll then hear two short sets by small ensembles of expert musicians from a range of musical backgrounds, each exploring spontaneous and unscripted ways of making music together. The night ends with “Switchemups”: a fun, low-pressure session where audience members are welcome to join the musicians on stage and try improvising themselves (totally optional!). Expect an evening of surprising sounds, creative energy, and a warm, welcoming atmosphere.

events.title: De Profundis: Oscar Wilde in Jail

venue.name: Soulpepper Theatre
venue.address: 50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4

events.description: “There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”
events.details: “There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.” This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession. In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop. Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us. Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th Get your tickets today https://soulpepper.ca/whats-on/de-profundis-oscar-wilde-in-jail/ !

events.details: Since 2021, the Fusion Festival has brought together writers, directors and actors to workshop and develop new works by Canadian playwrights & screenwriters. Building on this tradition, we’re proud to introduce The Fusion Lab, a new initiative dedicated to supporting Canadian artists through year-round workshops designed to facilitate the creation of new Canadian works. The program will provide opportunities for artists to develop their work, with selected scripts showcase at our annual Fusion Festival! This season, we’re excited to present staged readings of two original Canadian plays written by Brandon Nicoletti. SPOTTER Featuring: Patrick S. McEwen & Blake Pyne When Kai nearly injures himself during a bench press, Tyler steps in and offers to be his spotter. The two men form an unlikely connection that sparks conversations about body image, modern dating, and the way gay men see each other. KILL TEST Featuring: Marisa Roggeveen, Andy Kalirai, & Scott Clark A rookie operative must extract information from a captive while her mentor tests her resolve. Join us at Naturlandia on November 27 th at 8:30pm for an evening of new Canadian theatre.

events.details: clay pigeon clay pigeon is the songwriting project of Canadian musician James Clayton. It is also a band and collection of friends based in Montreal who make music together. Their sophomore album, Cash Out in Kid Gloves, is built around the tension between human performance and synthetic intervention. Recorded between a residency in Woburn, Quebec, a nineteenth-century heritage home in Peterborough, Ontario, and additional sessions in Montreal, the band focused on capturing the imperfections of musicians playing together live, then deliberately disrupted those performances with processing, edits, and obvious post production. As technology increasingly blurs the line between what's human and machine made, Cash Out in Kid Gloves explores that uncertainty by wrapping an alt-country/folk rock band in synthetic layers. Bandcamp Instagram Website Ultra Far Emerging from the ashes of Canadian band Property (2016-2021), Ultra Far is the new alternative project of St. John’s & Montreal-based Sarah Harris. Ultra Far is an experimentation of sound and genre: simultaneously electronic and organic; optimistic and wistful.

events.details: yo yo oto presents... Daniel Bell Trustfall Hiroki ~~~~~~ Daniel Bell stands as one of electronic music’s most influential minimalists. Emerging from Detroit in the early 1990s, Bell developed a radically stripped-down language of rhythm, repetition and funk that helped shape the course of minimal house and techno worldwide. As DBX, he created a series of landmark recordings, most notably 1994’s “Losing Control”—a hypnotic underground anthem whose influence continues to resonate across generations of producers and DJs. Behind the decks, Bell is a master of reduction: precise, patient and relentlessly funky, building dance floors through subtle shifts rather than obvious gestures. More than three decades into his career, he remains one of the few Detroit originals still pushing minimal electronic music forward on his own unmistakable terms. Trustfall is a Toronto-based artist, radio host and organizer. They have a soft spot for eclectic, left-handed selections and oddball psychedelia across all genres. They organize a bi-monthly party series called Freakers Corner at Bampot House in Toronto with their collective Freakers Union.

events.description: THE LAST ONE OF THE YEAR.
events.details: THE LAST ONE OF THE YEAR. One more night before the year runs out. CNSRED closes 2026 at Bunker with three DJs, techno from the first track to the last, and a dance floor with no screens on it. Friday, November 27. Doors at 10 PM. We go until late. CNSRED is a Berlin-inspired underground techno event and a sanctuary for freedom, expression, and pure connection. Built by and for the 2SLGBTQ+ community, this is queer energy in motion where the music runs deep, the lights stay low, and the focus is strictly on the sound. Expect hypnotic techno and dark, driving house rhythms that carry you from late night into early morning. From the opening track to the final beat, the warehouse transforms into a layered landscape of sound and movement. Every beat invites you to move differently, every corner offers a new sonic experience, and the crowd is open, expressive, and alive. 🚫 No phones. 🚫 No cameras. 🚫 No distractions. Be present. Be immersed. What happens on the floor stays on the floor. Without screens, we create space for genuine connection, shared energy, and full freedom. Your experience is yours alone — dance, listen, move, rest, and explore at your own pace.

events.description: “Wear something shiny. Put your phone away.”
events.details: “Wear something shiny. Put your phone away.” Hello, gorgeous. Fix your lipstick, because we’re going back to the golden age of disco, when a velvet rope was the only thing standing between you and the best night of your life. (Don’t worry, you’re on the list. Everyone’s on the list. We’re not monsters.) SUGAR RUSH Disco Toronto is a queer-forward dance experience celebrating the shimmering worlds of nu-disco and old school disco, where glittering rhythms, deep grooves, and pulsing basslines come together for a night built entirely around movement and release. Think 1977, but with better lighting and fewer regrets. Step into a high-energy atmosphere of glowing lights, immersive sound, and a dance floor that never lets up. From warm, funky disco textures to driving, the music is designed to keep bodies moving and spirits lifted from the first track to the last. Our mirror ball has been working out and is ready to be seen. This is more than a party. It’s a space for expression, connection, and joy on the dance floor. Music lovers, dancers, and night wanderers come together under one roof to sweat, sparkle, and lose themselves in the sound. Yes, you will sweat.

events.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming shoe museum. Located in Toronto, Canada, the Bata Shoe Museum regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artifacts, chosen from a collection of nearly 15,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. events.details: From November 21 to December 3, join the 7th Mulan International Film Festival at Toronto’s Innis Town Hall. As the largest film festival dedicated to Chinese-language cinema in North America, Mulan brings restored classics and new voices to the big screen. Opening night presents the Canadian premiere of the 4K restoration of Patrick TAM’s Love Massacre, starring Brigitte LIN. The festival closes with the North American premiere of CHONG Keat Aun’s Golden Horse Award-winning Mother Bhumi, winner of Best Leading Actress for FAN Bingbing, Best Cinematography and Best Original Film Song. Discover six features and nine shorts from emerging filmmakers in the Fountainhead competition programme, and vote for your favourites. Other highlights include the world premiere of the new 4K restoration of Clara LAW’s Farewell, China, starring Maggie CHEUNG and Tony LEUNG Ka-Fai, and On Canvas, On Stage, a complete retrospective of QIU Jiongjiong’s films, including A New Old Play and Madame. Festival Packs and individual tickets, starting at $10 plus processing fees, are now on sale. Screening times vary by day.

events.details: Two films, one afternoon of radical music, art and New York counterculture. Films We Like presents a special double feature of FUGS FILM and NOVA '78 at Paradise Theatre on November 28, featuring two Q&As with film critic Jason Gorber. FUGS FILM, directed by Chuck Smith, chronicles The Fugs, the legendary 1960s underground rock band whose provocative music fused poetry, politics and anti-establishment rebellion. NOVA '78, directed by Aaron Brookner and Rodrigo Areias, transports audiences to the legendary 1978 Nova Convention in New York City. Built from rediscovered archival footage, the film captures a remarkable gathering of countercultural icons including William S. Burroughs, Patti Smith, Frank Zappa, Allen Ginsberg and Laurie Anderson. Join us for an afternoon celebrating the artists, musicians and troublemakers who helped reshape American culture.

events.description: “There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”
events.details: “There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.” This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession. In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop. Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us. Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th Get your tickets today https://soulpepper.ca/whats-on/de-profundis-oscar-wilde-in-jail/ !

events.details: “There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.” This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession. In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop. Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us. events.title: Free Sunday
events.description: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming and surprising shoe museum. Located in Toronto, the Bata Shoe Museum (BSM) regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artefacts, chosen from a collection of almost 14,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-wi…
events.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming and surprising shoe museum. Located in Toronto, the Bata Shoe Museum (BSM) regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artefacts, chosen from a collection of almost 14,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. Over 4,500 years of history are reflected in our permanent exhibition, All About Shoes while our three other galleries feature changing exhibitions. Over the course of this year we will continuing to present The Great Divide: Footwear in the Age of Enlightenment and our newest exhibit, All Dolled Up: Fashioning Cultural Expectations explores how dolls and the clothes they wear have historically promoted complex cultural ideas about gender, body image, social status and fashion consumption in the West and how these ideas are being challenged today.

events.details: “There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.” This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession. In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop. Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us. events.details: From November 21 to December 3, join the 7th Mulan International Film Festival at Toronto’s Innis Town Hall. As the largest film festival dedicated to Chinese-language cinema in North America, Mulan brings restored classics and new voices to the big screen. Opening night presents the Canadian premiere of the 4K restoration of Patrick TAM’s Love Massacre, starring Brigitte LIN. The festival closes with the North American premiere of CHONG Keat Aun’s Golden Horse Award-winning Mother Bhumi, winner of Best Leading Actress for FAN Bingbing, Best Cinematography and Best Original Film Song. Discover six features and nine shorts from emerging filmmakers in the Fountainhead competition programme, and vote for your favourites. Other highlights include the world premiere of the new 4K restoration of Clara LAW’s Farewell, China, starring Maggie CHEUNG and Tony LEUNG Ka-Fai, and On Canvas, On Stage, a complete retrospective of QIU Jiongjiong’s films, including A New Old Play and Madame. Festival Packs and individual tickets, starting at $10 plus processing fees, are now on sale. Screening times vary by day.

events.details: Curly-coated Devon Rex kittens, easy beginner yoga, and the cure for the Sunday scaries in Toronto. Mats provided. The Sunday scaries don't stand a chance against a lapful of curly-coated kittens. Welcome to Devon Rex Kitten Yoga by Yoga Kawa in Toronto, where the playlist is soft, the poses are beginner-friendly, and the kittens have absolutely no respect for your personal space. In the best possible way. Devon Rex kittens are small, warm, and wildly social. They tend to climb onto shoulders, tuck into necks, and purr directly into ears. Consider yourself warned. Here's how the hour breaks down: 35 minutes of easy, beginner-friendly yoga 20 minutes of connection and cuddle time with the kittens 5 minutes of sharing circle Why people keep coming back Kitten yoga has a way of making the room soften. You arrive carrying the weight of the week, a kitten headbutts your chin, and your nervous system just... exhales. It sounds simple because it is, and that's exactly the point. A note on Devon Rex kittens Devon Rex cats are often called the pixies of the cat world, and it tracks. They are highly social, deeply curious, and unusually warm to the touch thanks to their fine, wavy coats.

events.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming shoe museum. Located in Toronto, Canada, the Bata Shoe Museum regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artifacts, chosen from a collection of nearly 15,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. Over 4,500 years of history are reflected in our permanent exhibition, All About Shoes while our three other galleries feature changing exhibitions – so there’s always something new to see.

events.details: From November 21 to December 3, join the 7th Mulan International Film Festival at Toronto’s Innis Town Hall. As the largest film festival dedicated to Chinese-language cinema in North America, Mulan brings restored classics and new voices to the big screen. Opening night presents the Canadian premiere of the 4K restoration of Patrick TAM’s Love Massacre, starring Brigitte LIN. The festival closes with the North American premiere of CHONG Keat Aun’s Golden Horse Award-winning Mother Bhumi, winner of Best Leading Actress for FAN Bingbing, Best Cinematography and Best Original Film Song. Discover six features and nine shorts from emerging filmmakers in the Fountainhead competition programme, and vote for your favourites. Other highlights include the world premiere of the new 4K restoration of Clara LAW’s Farewell, China, starring Maggie CHEUNG and Tony LEUNG Ka-Fai, and On Canvas, On Stage, a complete retrospective of QIU Jiongjiong’s films, including A New Old Play and Madame. Festival Packs and individual tickets, starting at $10 plus processing fees, are now on sale. Screening times vary by day.

events.title: Curator's Talk: Stitching Status - Time, Labour, and the Value of Beads
events.description: Beads may be small and intricate, but their histories reveal powerful stories of identity, value, and status. In celebration of One Bead After Another: Beaded Footwear From Around the World , join Director & Senior Curator Elizabeth Semmelhack for an informative and illuminating exploration of beadw…
events.details: Beads may be small and intricate, but their histories reveal powerful stories of identity, value, and status. In celebration of One Bead After Another: Beaded Footwear From Around the World , join Director & Senior Curator Elizabeth Semmelhack for an informative and illuminating exploration of beadwork traditions from around the world, and their role as markers of wealth, prestige, and cultural meaning. From royal adornment and ceremonial regalia to trade and personal expression, this lecture traces how beads have signaled belonging across time and place. At its core is the labour behind the work: the skilled craftsmanship, generational knowledge, and cultural practices embedded in every stitch. By centering time and labour, the talk challenges conventional ideas of value—asking what makes something “luxurious,” and who defines it. Through cross-cultural perspectives and historical insight, this talk reframes beadwork as more than decoration, as a powerful language of status, resilience, and artistry.

events.details: WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage! Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan. Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures. Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto. Written and Directed by Tien Providence Performance by Drae Walsh Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling. 🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet. Live Theatre. Live History.

events.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming shoe museum. Located in Toronto, Canada, the Bata Shoe Museum regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artifacts, chosen from a collection of nearly 15,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. Over 4,500 years of history are reflected in our permanent exhibition, All About Shoes while our three other galleries feature changing exhibitions – so there’s always something new to see.

events.details: From November 21 to December 3, join the 7th Mulan International Film Festival at Toronto’s Innis Town Hall. As the largest film festival dedicated to Chinese-language cinema in North America, Mulan brings restored classics and new voices to the big screen. Opening night presents the Canadian premiere of the 4K restoration of Patrick TAM’s Love Massacre, starring Brigitte LIN. The festival closes with the North American premiere of CHONG Keat Aun’s Golden Horse Award-winning Mother Bhumi, winner of Best Leading Actress for FAN Bingbing, Best Cinematography and Best Original Film Song. Discover six features and nine shorts from emerging filmmakers in the Fountainhead competition programme, and vote for your favourites. Other highlights include the world premiere of the new 4K restoration of Clara LAW’s Farewell, China, starring Maggie CHEUNG and Tony LEUNG Ka-Fai, and On Canvas, On Stage, a complete retrospective of QIU Jiongjiong’s films, including A New Old Play and Madame. Festival Packs and individual tickets, starting at $10 plus processing fees, are now on sale. Screening times vary by day.

events.details: WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage! Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan. Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures. Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto. Written and Directed by Tien Providence Performance by Drae Walsh Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling. 🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet. Live Theatre. Live History.

The Cape Breton band has earned rave reviews from audiences around the world and an impressive list of credits for their recordings, Rove (2017), Carols (2015) and Five (2014), including a Canadian Folk Music Award, a JUNO Award nomination and multiple East Coast Music Awards and Music Nova Scotia Awards. events.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming shoe museum. Located in Toronto, Canada, the Bata Shoe Museum regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artifacts, chosen from a collection of nearly 15,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. Over 4,500 years of history are reflected in our permanent exhibition, All About Shoes while our three other galleries feature changing exhibitions – so there’s always something new to see.

events.details: From November 21 to December 3, join the 7th Mulan International Film Festival at Toronto’s Innis Town Hall. As the largest film festival dedicated to Chinese-language cinema in North America, Mulan brings restored classics and new voices to the big screen. Opening night presents the Canadian premiere of the 4K restoration of Patrick TAM’s Love Massacre, starring Brigitte LIN. The festival closes with the North American premiere of CHONG Keat Aun’s Golden Horse Award-winning Mother Bhumi, winner of Best Leading Actress for FAN Bingbing, Best Cinematography and Best Original Film Song. Discover six features and nine shorts from emerging filmmakers in the Fountainhead competition programme, and vote for your favourites. Other highlights include the world premiere of the new 4K restoration of Clara LAW’s Farewell, China, starring Maggie CHEUNG and Tony LEUNG Ka-Fai, and On Canvas, On Stage, a complete retrospective of QIU Jiongjiong’s films, including A New Old Play and Madame. Festival Packs and individual tickets, starting at $10 plus processing fees, are now on sale. Screening times vary by day.

events.description: WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!
events.details: WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage! Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan. Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures. Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto. Written and Directed by Tien Providence Performance by Drae Walsh Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling. 🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet. Live Theatre. Live History.

events.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming shoe museum. Located in Toronto, Canada, the Bata Shoe Museum regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artifacts, chosen from a collection of nearly 15,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. Over 4,500 years of history are reflected in our permanent exhibition, All About Shoes while our three other galleries feature changing exhibitions – so there’s always something new to see.

events.details: WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage! Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan. Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures. Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto. Written and Directed by Tien Providence Performance by Drae Walsh Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling. 🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet. Live Theatre. Live History.

events.description: A Christmas Carol like you've never seen it before!
events.details: A Christmas Carol like you've never seen it before! The critically acclaimed holiday comedy INVASION: CHRISTMAS CAROL returns to The Assembly Theatre in Toronto this December. It starts with six actors performing Dickens' classic tale of Ebenezer Scrooge. But about five minutes into the show, a surprise guest "Invader" crashes the story as a character of their own creation. events.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming shoe museum. Located in Toronto, Canada, the Bata Shoe Museum regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artifacts, chosen from a collection of nearly 15,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. Over 4,500 years of history are reflected in our permanent exhibition, All About Shoes while our three other galleries feature changing exhibitions – so there’s always something new to see.

events.description: WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!
events.details: WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage! Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan. Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures. Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto. Written and Directed by Tien Providence Performance by Drae Walsh Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling. 🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet. Live Theatre. Live History.

events.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming shoe museum. Located in Toronto, Canada, the Bata Shoe Museum regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artifacts, chosen from a collection of nearly 15,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. Over 4,500 years of history are reflected in our permanent exhibition, All About Shoes while our three other galleries feature changing exhibitions – so there’s always something new to see.

As AI filmmaking gains momentum in Toronto and across Canada, GenTO provides a platform for the growing community of creators to showcase their work, exchange ideas and connect with industry professionals. events.description: WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!
events.details: WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage! Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan. Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures. Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto. Written and Directed by Tien Providence Performance by Drae Walsh Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling. 🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet. Live Theatre. Live History.

events.description: WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!
events.details: WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage! Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan. Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures. Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto. Written and Directed by Tien Providence Performance by Drae Walsh Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling. 🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet. Live Theatre. Live History.

events.description: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming and surprising shoe museum. events.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming and surprising shoe museum. Located in Toronto, the Bata Shoe Museum (BSM) regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artefacts, chosen from a collection of almost 14,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. Over 4,500 years of history are reflected in our permanent exhibition, All About Shoes while our three other galleries feature changing exhibitions. Over the course of this year we will continuing to present The Great Divide: Footwear in the Age of Enlightenment and our newest exhibit, All Dolled Up: Fashioning Cultural Expectations explores how dolls and the clothes they wear have historically promoted complex cultural ideas about gender, body image, social status and fashion consumption in the West and how these ideas are being challenged today.

events.details: WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage! Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan. Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures. Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto. Written and Directed by Tien Providence Performance by Drae Walsh Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling. 🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet. Live Theatre. Live History.

Located in Toronto, Canada, the Bata Shoe Museum regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artifacts, chosen from a collection of nearly 15,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. events.details: Tracy Michailidis Live in the Green Sanderson Hall at Hugh's Room, 296 Broadview Avenue Show at 7:30pm, Doors at 7:00pm $35+ in advance, $42+ at the door, $25+ student, arts worker, underemployed ticket Seven years ago, Tracy did a show at the Jazz Bistro she was set to reprise in the Spring of 2020. The show was cancelled. And life was forever altered. This cabaret explores the time that was, the time that is , and the moments in between. Joined by Noreen Waibel at the piano and Liza McClellan on cello, Dora-award winning actress Tracy Michailidis explores themes of time, love, and crossword puzzles. Featuring music by folks like Stephen Sondheim, Lennon and McCartney, Joni Mitchell, and Kurt Weill , this evening is about finding a little light in the dark. TRACY MICHAILIDIS is an award-winning singer and actor who has spent her career gracing stages across Canada, on Broadway and on National Tours, and across Europe. Last seen in the all-Yiddish production of Fiddler on the Roof at the Elgin Theatre, she also runs her own coaching studio, is passionate about developing new work, and loves the Toronto Blue Jays.

events.description: Let's sip, stitch, and get into the holiday spirit!🧶🎄🧋 The Crochet and Knit Club is partnering with The Alley to host our first ever event, the Holiday Boba Social! Join us on December 8, 2026, at 4:00 PM (EST) at George Brown Polythechnic's St.
events.details: Let's sip, stitch, and get into the holiday spirit!🧶🎄🧋 The Crochet and Knit Club is partnering with The Alley to host our first ever event, the Holiday Boba Social! Join us on December 8, 2026, at 4:00 PM (EST) at George Brown Polythechnic's St. James Campus for bubble tea, cheerful holiday music, and meeting new people. Whether you’re a curious beginner or a seasoned crafter with a few too many projects on the go, you’re welcome here! Bring along your crochet or knitting project, get inspired to make something festive, or simply settle in and enjoy the company. And if your idea of a perfect study break is sipping boba and chatting, we’d love to have you, too. You don’t need to make anything to join the fun—this is a chance to step away from exam stress, meet fellow students, and enjoy a little holiday cheer. Come with friends or come on your own, wear something cozy, and spend some time unwinding with us. We can’t wait to see you there! ✨

events.details: Bluegrass Christmas with The Barrel Boys On Tuesday, December 8th, celebrate the holiday season with The Barrel Boys' Bluegrass Christmas show at Burdock, featuring enchanting melodies and heartwarming harmonies that bring a delightful blend of folk, bluegrass, and Americana to your Christmas festivities. From timeless carols to original compositions, their music captures the season's essence, infusing every note with warmth and memory. Join The Barrel Boys for a magical event that will fill your heart with joy and leave you with cherished memories of the most beautiful time of the year. The Barrel Boys are a unique staple of Canadian roots music - a bluegrass powerhouse featuring rich vocal harmonies, killer picking, and a fun-loving, down-to-earth stage presence. Informed by the deep traditions of bluegrass, country, old-time, and Americana, The Boys have crafted their unmistakable sound into an exuberant and deeply soulful musical experience. Throughout more than a decade of performing together, The Barrel Boys’ bluegrass Christmas concert has been an important part of their holiday season.

events.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming shoe museum. Located in Toronto, Canada, the Bata Shoe Museum regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artifacts, chosen from a collection of nearly 15,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. Over 4,500 years of history are reflected in our permanent exhibition, All About Shoes while our three other galleries feature changing exhibitions – so there’s always something new to see.

events.title: Glitter in the Archives
events.description: Glitter in the Archives: reference materials for re-creation
events.details: Glitter in the Archives: reference materials for re-creation In this talk, Ian Danger Capstick traces his practice of quilting using The ArQuives’ and other archival photographic collections as reference. He recreates protest signs and banners, ephemeral objects often made to last only an afternoon, as quilted objects you can hold today. His talk introduces artists and thinkers who have influenced his work and who invented, fabricated and quilted their own queer ancestry when the record came up empty. Glitter here is literal (polyester, metallic thread, a conservator’s nightmare), metaphorical (evidence that refuses to behave) and finally a call to action: create sparkle, save your ephemera, support your community archivist and treat our local archives and museums as essential infrastructure. December 9, 2026 6:00PM - 7:30PM The ArQuives, Toronto PWYC, 5$ suggested, Registration Required: arquives.ca/event/glitter-in-the-archives

events.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming shoe museum. Located in Toronto, Canada, the Bata Shoe Museum regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artifacts, chosen from a collection of nearly 15,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. Over 4,500 years of history are reflected in our permanent exhibition, All About Shoes while our three other galleries feature changing exhibitions – so there’s always something new to see.

events.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming shoe museum. Located in Toronto, Canada, the Bata Shoe Museum regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artifacts, chosen from a collection of nearly 15,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. Over 4,500 years of history are reflected in our permanent exhibition, All About Shoes while our three other galleries feature changing exhibitions – so there’s always something new to see.

Every second Friday of the month we've remained open until 9 pm (we usually close at 5 pm!) for all to enjoy, with special free programming new each week plus access to all current exhibitions . This week: Collage Holiday Cards Design your own holiday cards inspired by the colours, textures, and stories on display at the museum. Whether you’re crafting heartfelt messages for loved ones or simply getting into the festive spirit, this relaxed drop-in program offers a perfect blend of creativity, reflection, and fun. No experience needed, and all materials are provided. Drop in, have some fun, and take home your own design. events.details: Boreal Live in the Green Sanderson Hall at Hugh's Room, 296 Broadview Avenue Show at 8pm, Doors at 7pm $35+ in advance, $42+ at the door Boreal is a powerhouse trio of Canadian singer-songwriters—Tannis Slimmon, Angie Nussey, and Katherine Wheatley. Their new album, “Winterbirds” (March 2025), has earned them Canadian Folk Music Award nominations for Album of the Year, Ensemble of the Year, and Vocal Group of the Year. Katherine brings warmth, colour, and rhythm on guitar; Tannis holds the heartbeat on percussion, mandolin, and guitar; and Angie adds rich textures on keyboard. With no designated lead singer, Boreal rotates the spotlight, offering a fresh approach to every song through thoughtful arrangements and harmonies. Their music weaves three distinct voices—Katherine’s is deep, steady and rooted in earthy folk; Tannis’s is ethereal, improvisational and explores sacred soundscapes; Angie is the emotional, untamed force. When they write and arrange their songs, they take advantage of these differences. The result is a unique sound that's as cohesive as it is surprising.

events.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming shoe museum. Located in Toronto, Canada, the Bata Shoe Museum regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artifacts, chosen from a collection of nearly 15,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. Over 4,500 years of history are reflected in our permanent exhibition, All About Shoes while our three other galleries feature changing exhibitions – so there’s always something new to see.

events.details: Yorkie puppies, easy beginner yoga, and the Saturday you've been meaning to take back in Toronto. Mats provided. Halloween afternoon, and you're spending it with Yorkie puppies. Honestly, best decision you've made all month. Welcome to Yorkie Puppy Yoga by Yoga Kawa in Toronto! Enjoy one hour of beginner-friendly yoga surrounded by a tiny crew of Yorkshire Terrier puppies who have big personalities and absolutely no concept of personal space. Yorkies may be small, but their confidence is larger than life! Expect curious little faces, playful zoomies, tiny paws exploring your mat, and plenty of puppy cuddles. Don’t be surprised if one of these adorable little companions decides your yoga pose is the perfect place for a snuggle. 🐶🤎 Here's how the hour breaks down: 35 minutes of easy, beginner-friendly yoga 20 minutes of connection and cuddle time 5 minutes of sharing circle Why people keep coming back Puppy yoga in Toronto does something a regular yoga class cannot. Honestly, best decision you've made all month. Welcome to Yorkie Puppy Yoga by Yoga Kawa in Toronto! Enjoy one hour of beginner-friendly yoga surrounded by a tiny crew of Yorkshire Terrier puppies who have big personalities and absolutely no concept of personal space. Yorkies may be small, but their confidence is larger than life! Expect curious little faces, playful zoomies, tiny paws exploring your mat, and plenty of puppy cuddles. events.title: Songs of My Mother: A Celebration of African Women Concert

venue.name: The Redwood
venue.address: 1300 Gerrard St E, Toronto, ON M4L 1Y7

events.description: Batuki Music Society presents Songs of My Mother: A Celebration of African Women at the Redwood Theatre on Saturday December 12th at 8 pm. Doors open at 7 pm.
events.details: Batuki Music Society presents Songs of My Mother: A Celebration of African Women at the Redwood Theatre on Saturday December 12th at 8 pm. Doors open at 7 pm. Three electrifying vocalists and a dancer with roots on the African continent will honour the role of women and mothers in carrying on musical traditions. Songs of My Mother: A Celebration of African Women, curated by Batuki Music Society will showcase diverse stories and musical styles from different regions of sub-Saharan Africa. Featured will be JUNO Award winners, South African-born Lorraine Klaasen and Malian-born Djely Tapa, also on the line-up is Melat Mengesha, winner of the Balageru (Ethiopian Idol) and Guinea-born dancer Mabinty Sylla. These women share their unique talents in a showcase of musical diversity and artistic excellence, supported by an ensemble of accomplished musicians from Toronto and Montreal. This presentation shines a light on female singers and their significance in African customs, rituals and ceremonies. The first words or language that a child hears from their mother are often shared in song.

events.description: Join us at Friends House for an evening of exploratory sound art performance, in a triple-bill bringing together distinct builders of the form—Devin DiSanto, Anne-F Jacques, and Shadow Pattern, featuring installation art by Izzy Mink of Tümmler Studio.
events.details: PWYC Join us at Friends House for an evening of exploratory sound art performance, in a triple-bill bringing together distinct builders of the form—Devin DiSanto, Anne-F Jacques, and Shadow Pattern, featuring installation art by Izzy Mink of Tümmler Studio. Stringing together sonic elements of the everyday into ideations and completions of tasks, Devin DiSanto visits from New York, pushing the conceptual bounds of how electroacoustic sounds are created and performed. We are also joined by the acute material tinkerings of Anne-F Jacques (Montréal) and the paint-stripped tape ripples of Shadow Pattern (Hamilton), for a night of three subtle solo sets bridging active listening with experimental performance. As a textural complement to the live sets, the evening will also feature the installation ‘Persistent Feeder’, by Izzy Mink of Tümmler Studio. Co-presented and curated by the Ministry of Phonic Services, a Toronto-based concert presenter and experimental record label. If cost is a barrier, please reach out to us at sara@musicgallery.org mailto:sara@musicgallery.org to reserve a lower-priced PWYC ticket at the door. events.description: Songs of Christmas and Francey Fan Favourites. David Francey Live in the Green Sanderson Hall at Hugh's Room, 296 Broadview Avenue Show at 8pm, Doors at 7pm $65+ in advance, $72+ at the door David Francey: A Christmas Gathering.
events.details: David Francey Live in the Green Sanderson Hall at Hugh's Room, 296 Broadview Avenue Show at 8pm, Doors at 7pm $65+ in advance, $72+ at the door David Francey: A Christmas Gathering. Songs of Christmas, and Francey fan favorites from over the years David Francey is a Scottish-born Canadian carpenter turned songwriter, who has become known as “one of Canada’s most revered folk poets and singers” – Toronto Star . A truly authentic folk singer, Francey is a documentarian of the working person who never imagined earning a living from his music. When he was in his 40s, his wife, artist Beth Girdler, encouraged him to share his songs and sing in public. The reaction was instant. His first album, Torn Screen Door, came out in 1999 and was a hit in Canada. Since then, he has released eleven albums, won three JUNO Awards and has had his songs covered by such artists as The Del McCoury Band, The Rankin Family, James Keelaghan and Tracy Grammer. In concert, David is a singer and a storyteller. He returns to Hugh’s Room on Saturday December 12 .

events.description: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming and surprising shoe museum. Located in Toronto, the Bata Shoe Museum (BSM) regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artefacts, chosen from a collection of almost 14,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-wi…
events.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming and surprising shoe museum. Located in Toronto, the Bata Shoe Museum (BSM) regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artefacts, chosen from a collection of almost 14,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. Over 4,500 years of history are reflected in our permanent exhibition, All About Shoes while our three other galleries feature changing exhibitions. Over the course of this year we will continuing to present The Great Divide: Footwear in the Age of Enlightenment and our newest exhibit, All Dolled Up: Fashioning Cultural Expectations explores how dolls and the clothes they wear have historically promoted complex cultural ideas about gender, body image, social status and fashion consumption in the West and how these ideas are being challenged today.

December 13th, 2026 // 6pm // $20 all prices + fees Whatever Happened to Baby Jane? an [interrupted] screening with Ronnie Burkett and Daniel MacIvor, joined by ted witzel as director (referee) and blessings to Bette & Joan Really th…
events.details: December 13th, 2026 // 6pm // $20 all prices + fees Whatever Happened to Baby Jane? an [interrupted] screening with Ronnie Burkett and Daniel MacIvor, joined by ted witzel as director (referee) and blessings to Bette & Joan Really though, whatever did happen to Baby Jane? Queer performance legends Daniel MacIvor and Ronnie Burkett are diving deep into the camp canon, with a new piece in the works inspired by the cult classic, Whatever Happened to Baby Jane? Join us for an epic first workshop of something new we’re cooking up—the very first (very chaotic) step of the process. It’s kind of a film screening, but also an unhinged evening at Buddies’ Cabaret where Burkett, MacIvor and witzel watch the film, press pause whenever they like, and randomly start vibing, workshopping, and descending into madness about whatever this new thing is that they are going to create. Unscripted, unhinged, and we don’t even know if we have the literary rights to be doing this. Come be part of this work as it's being developed from day one. Popcorn will be served, bar will be open. Dress festive with vengeance in your heart.

events.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming shoe museum. Located in Toronto, Canada, the Bata Shoe Museum regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artifacts, chosen from a collection of nearly 15,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. events.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming shoe museum. Located in Toronto, Canada, the Bata Shoe Museum regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artifacts, chosen from a collection of nearly 15,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. Over 4,500 years of history are reflected in our permanent exhibition, All About Shoes while our three other galleries feature changing exhibitions – so there’s always something new to see.

events.title: Curator's Talk: A Look Into André Perugia
events.description: Step behind the scenes of André Perugia: A Design Legend Unveiled for a curator talk with Nishi Bassi, who will share how the exhibition came together – from sourcing rare loans to the curatorial decisions that shaped the many intricate design and storytelling elements.
events.details: Step behind the scenes of André Perugia: A Design Legend Unveiled for a curator talk with Nishi Bassi, who will share how the exhibition came together – from sourcing rare loans to the curatorial decisions that shaped the many intricate design and storytelling elements. Discover how Perugia’s innovative designs revolutionized footwear through bold experimentation, architectural form, and technical mastery, and how, nearly a century later, Perugia’s designs continue to influence fashion’s most daring creators. About Nishi Bassi Nishi Bassi, Curator and Exhibitions Project Manager at the Bata Shoe Museum, brings over 10 years of experience in the museum industry. Her educational background is in British history, and current research interests include fashion, consumer culture, and post-colonialism. She is also an EDI champion who strategically plans and advocates for change to ensure that accessibility remains a priority in all projects. Nishi has been with the Bata Shoe Museum since 2013, where she currently works as the Curator and Manager of Exhibitions. She also holds a volunteer position on the Board of Directors for ICOM Canada.

events.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming shoe museum. Located in Toronto, Canada, the Bata Shoe Museum regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artifacts, chosen from a collection of nearly 15,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. Over 4,500 years of history are reflected in our permanent exhibition, All About Shoes while our three other galleries feature changing exhibitions – so there’s always something new to see.

events.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming shoe museum. Located in Toronto, Canada, the Bata Shoe Museum regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artifacts, chosen from a collection of nearly 15,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. Over 4,500 years of history are reflected in our permanent exhibition, All About Shoes while our three other galleries feature changing exhibitions – so there’s always something new to see.

events.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming shoe museum. Located in Toronto, Canada, the Bata Shoe Museum regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artifacts, chosen from a collection of nearly 15,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. Over 4,500 years of history are reflected in our permanent exhibition, All About Shoes while our three other galleries feature changing exhibitions – so there’s always something new to see.

All net proceeds from this concert will be donated to “Inclusion Without Limits” NGO (Ukraine) to help rebuild the Specialized Children’s Centre “Colibri” in Kremenchuk, Ukraine, which was destroyed in a Russian attack on November 8, 2026 . Friday, December 18, 2026 7:30 PM (Doors 7:00 PM) Heliconian Hall 35 Hazelton Avenue, Toronto, ON Performers DIVKA DIVKA is bandurist (esoteric Ukrainian harp) Alina Kuzma and violist (not a violin) Zoë Santo. In 2024, she released two acclaimed albums: Show Love , an innovative EP that builds new sonic ground while honouring the sounds of her previous six studio projects; and Winter Song , a full-length celebration of holiday music that earned a 2025 JUNO nomination for Vocal Jazz Album of the Year. With nine albums to her name, including a celebrated tribute to Nina Simone, Kellylee Evans continues to captivate audiences with a mix of heartfelt originals and timeless classics. Join us on Friday December 18 for an unforgettable night of music that celebrates the holidays and the power of a truly extraordinary voice.

events.description: Fluffy Bichon Frise puppies, beginner-friendly yoga, and the cure for the Sunday scaries in Toronto. Mats provided. The Sunday scaries do not stand a chance against a Bichon Frise puppy. Welcome to Bichon Frise Puppy Yoga by Yoga Kawa in Toronto.
events.details: Fluffy Bichon Frise puppies, beginner-friendly yoga, and the cure for the Sunday scaries in Toronto. Mats provided. The Sunday scaries do not stand a chance against a Bichon Frise puppy. Welcome to Bichon Frise Puppy Yoga by Yoga Kawa in Toronto. This is a one-hour class where real puppies share your mat, your space, and honestly, most of your attention. Expect beginner-friendly movement, a lot of soft white fluff, and at least one moment where you forget what day it is. Bichons are compact, cloud-like, and absolutely convinced that every person in the room is their new best friend. They will find you. Here's how the hour breaks down: 35 minutes of easy, beginner-friendly yoga 20 minutes of connection and cuddle time 5 minutes of sharing circle Why people keep coming back Puppy yoga in Toronto does something a regular yoga class cannot. A puppy wanders over, settles against your leg, and your nervous system just... exhales. With Bichons specifically, that moment tends to come fast. They are warm, they are wiggly, and they have no concept of personal space, which on a Sunday morning is exactly the energy you need.

events.details: Fluffy Bichon Frise puppies, beginner-friendly yoga, and the cure for the Sunday scaries in Toronto. Mats provided. The Sunday scaries do not stand a chance against a Bichon Frise puppy. Welcome to Bichon Frise Puppy Yoga by Yoga Kawa in Toronto. This is a one-hour class where real puppies share your mat, your space, and honestly, most of your attention. Expect beginner-friendly movement, a lot of soft white fluff, and at least one moment where you forget what day it is. Bichons are compact, cloud-like, and absolutely convinced that every person in the room is their new best friend. They will find you. Here's how the hour breaks down: 35 minutes of easy, beginner-friendly yoga 20 minutes of connection and cuddle time 5 minutes of sharing circle Why people keep coming back Puppy yoga in Toronto does something a regular yoga class cannot. A puppy wanders over, settles against your leg, and your nervous system just... exhales. With Bichons specifically, that moment tends to come fast. They are warm, they are wiggly, and they have no concept of personal space, which on a Sunday morning is exactly the energy you need.

events.details: Cody Ellis is a Toronto based singer/songwriter blending folk, blues, country, and rock & roll into an authentic, roots driven sound. Known for his heartfelt songwriting, soulful vocals, and love of traditional Americana, Cody brings a new approach to modern roots music. With three solo albums under his belt, he’s now bringing his songs to life with a new band. Instagram Granny Smith is the singer-songwriter project of Jason Bhattacharya. After 2 decades touring as a session drummer (Bart, Blunt Chunks, Cozsmos Quartette, Dan Edmonds, Ferrari Garden, Julianna Riolino, Shirley Hurt, Shn Shn) and 5 seizures, Bhattacharya turned his art practice inward & began to create works of his own. Since 2020, he has released 5 singles, 4 music videos, 1 EP & in June of this year, ’Granthology,’ his debut LP. These recordings are produced, recorded, mixed, arranged & composed by Bhattacharya solely. “My grandparents were painters, I never got to meet them…they were prolific artists & the only contact I’ve had with them is through the work they left behind. I wanted to make a project where I could document my journey THROUGH music.” Instagram

events.details: Curly-coated Devon Rex kittens, easy beginner yoga, and the cure for the Sunday scaries in Toronto. Mats provided. The Sunday scaries don't stand a chance against a lapful of curly-coated kittens. Welcome to Devon Rex Kitten Yoga by Yoga Kawa in Toronto, where the playlist is soft, the poses are beginner-friendly, and the kittens have absolutely no respect for your personal space. In the best possible way. Devon Rex kittens are small, warm, and wildly social. They tend to climb onto shoulders, tuck into necks, and purr directly into ears. Consider yourself warned. Here's how the hour breaks down: 35 minutes of easy, beginner-friendly yoga 20 minutes of connection and cuddle time with the kittens 5 minutes of sharing circle Why people keep coming back Kitten yoga has a way of making the room soften. You arrive carrying the weight of the week, a kitten headbutts your chin, and your nervous system just... exhales. It sounds simple because it is, and that's exactly the point. A note on Devon Rex kittens Devon Rex cats are often called the pixies of the cat world, and it tracks. They are highly social, deeply curious, and unusually warm to the touch thanks to their fine, wavy coats.

events.details: The Glenn Paul Trio returns to the Burdock Music Hall for their cherished holiday show! 🎄 A Charlie Brown Christmas – A tribute to the music of Vince Guaraldi 🎄 A beloved holiday tradition returns! Glenn Paul Trio makes their return to The Burdock Music Hall (Toronto) to celebrate the timeless music of Vince Guaraldi’s iconic album A Charlie Brown Christmas . After performing 28 shows across Southern Ontario in 2025 , with multiple sold-out performances, the trio is bringing this cherished holiday favourite back to audiences for another season. Experience the music that has become the soundtrack to the holidays for generations. From the first beat of Linus and Lucy to the serene classic Christmas Time Is Here , the Glenn Paul Trio brings Guaraldi’s classic compositions to life with reverence and charm, while keeping their own musical fingerprint. More than just a concert, this is a chance to revisit the music that has defined childhood for generations. Think cozy living rooms and songs played on crackling vinyl , but performed live by an accomplished jazz trio.

events.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming and surprising shoe museum. Located in Toronto, the Bata Shoe Museum (BSM) regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artefacts, chosen from a collection of almost 14,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. Over 4,500 years of history are reflected in our permanent exhibition, All About Shoes while our three other galleries feature changing exhibitions. Over the course of this year we will continuing to present The Great Divide: Footwear in the Age of Enlightenment and our newest exhibit, All Dolled Up: Fashioning Cultural Expectations explores how dolls and the clothes they wear have historically promoted complex cultural ideas about gender, body image, social status and fashion consumption in the West and how these ideas are being challenged today.

events.details: Curly-coated Devon Rex kittens, easy beginner yoga, and the cure for the Sunday scaries in Toronto. Mats provided. The Sunday scaries don't stand a chance against a lapful of curly-coated kittens. Welcome to Devon Rex Kitten Yoga by Yoga Kawa in Toronto, where the playlist is soft, the poses are beginner-friendly, and the kittens have absolutely no respect for your personal space. In the best possible way. Devon Rex kittens are small, warm, and wildly social. They tend to climb onto shoulders, tuck into necks, and purr directly into ears. Consider yourself warned. Here's how the hour breaks down: 35 minutes of easy, beginner-friendly yoga 20 minutes of connection and cuddle time with the kittens 5 minutes of sharing circle Why people keep coming back Kitten yoga has a way of making the room soften. You arrive carrying the weight of the week, a kitten headbutts your chin, and your nervous system just... exhales. It sounds simple because it is, and that's exactly the point. A note on Devon Rex kittens Devon Rex cats are often called the pixies of the cat world, and it tracks. They are highly social, deeply curious, and unusually warm to the touch thanks to their fine, wavy coats.

Welcome to Bunny Yoga by Yoga Kawa in Toronto. This one is a little different from what most people picture when they hear the word yoga. The room is calmer.
events.details: Real live bunnies, gentle yoga, and the cure for the Sunday scaries in Toronto. Mats provided. The quietest hour you will have all week. Welcome to Bunny Yoga by Yoga Kawa in Toronto. This one is a little different from what most people picture when they hear the word yoga. The room is calmer. The music is softer. And the stars of the session move entirely on their own schedule. Bunnies are prey animals. They do not bound over the moment you unroll your mat. They read the room, assess the energy, and extend trust slowly. The class is built entirely around that pace. When a bunny chooses to hop over and settle beside you, it means something. That is the whole point. Here's how the hour breaks down: 35 minutes of easy, beginner-friendly yoga 20 minutes of quiet connection time, where the bunnies may approach you on their own terms 5 minutes of sharing circle Why people keep coming back Bunny yoga works because it asks everyone to slow down. Not in a forced, performative way. In the way that happens when a small animal decides you are safe enough to sit beside. Your breath evens out. Your shoulders drop. Your nervous system just... exhales.

events.description: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming and surprising shoe museum. Located in Toronto, the Bata Shoe Museum (BSM) regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artefacts, chosen from a collection of almost 14,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-wi…
events.details: Discover the treasures of North America’s inspiring, charming and surprising shoe museum. Located in Toronto, the Bata Shoe Museum (BSM) regularly displays over a thousand shoes and related artefacts, chosen from a collection of almost 14,000 objects, in architect Raymond Moriyama’s iconic, award-winning building. The BSM celebrates the style, development and function of footwear across four impressive galleries, with displays ranging from Chinese bound-foot shoes and ancient Egyptian sandals to chestnut-crushing clogs and glamorous platforms. Over 4,500 years of history are reflected in our permanent exhibition, All About Shoes while our three other galleries feature changing exhibitions. Over the course of this year we will continuing to present The Great Divide: Footwear in the Age of Enlightenment and our newest exhibit, All Dolled Up: Fashioning Cultural Expectations explores how dolls and the clothes they wear have historically promoted complex cultural ideas about gender, body image, social status and fashion consumption in the West and how these ideas are being challenged today.
