events.title: Daydreams Nye
events.description: DAYDREAMS returns this New Year’s Eve, bringing together Chicago’s Mark Grusane and hometown hero DJ Dirty Dale for a night where music leads, time disappears, and the dreams we’ve carried become the world we create.
events.details: DAYDREAMS returns this New Year’s Eve, bringing together Chicago’s Mark Grusane and hometown hero DJ Dirty Dale for a night where music leads, time disappears, and the dreams we’ve carried become the world we create. MARK GRUSANE (Chicago) A Chicago treasure whose relationship with the dancefloor stretches back to the ‘80s, Mark Grusane is a lifelong digger, producer, and co-founder of the legendary Mr. Peabody Records. With an encyclopedic knowledge of house, disco, and the musical worlds beyond, Mark has a rare instinct for what makes people move. His selections weave together obscure discoveries, timeless grooves, and unexpected diversions, creating deeply emotional journeys guided by a lifetime of musical curiosity and passion. DIRTY DALE (Toronto) A fixture in Toronto’s underground house community for over 25 years, Dirty Dale brings a dancer’s sensibility and a deep love for the groove to everything he plays. Rooted in the city’s soulful house tradition, his sound moves through deep, jazzy, Afro-influenced, and disco rhythms, blending forgotten gems with contemporary cuts.

events.details: YumYum is your home to move, explore, and connect. At its heart, this is a dance party—designed for queers to lose themselves in the music, the space, and their own desires. While we're proudly sex-positive, this is not exclusively a play party. It’s a space where consent is everything, and you’re free to express yourself however feels right—whether that means dancing all night, lounging with friends, or embracing moments of intimacy. From 10 PM to 7 AM, our multi-room, multi-floor venue transforms into an hazy playground of sound, movement, and possibility. No expectations, no pressure, no cameras—just the freedom to be unapologetically you.

events.title: Yoi Yoi Matsuri
events.description: Communal Japanese 'bon' dance party!. Yoi Yoi Matsuri: A Japanese Dance Party! Celebrate the opening of Nagata Shachu’s 29th anniversary 2026–2027 performance season with 'Yoi Yoi Matsuri' - a lively, welcoming evening of Japanese communal dancing and live music!
events.details: Yoi Yoi Matsuri: A Japanese Dance Party! Celebrate the opening of Nagata Shachu’s 29th anniversary 2026–2027 performance season with 'Yoi Yoi Matsuri' - a lively, welcoming evening of Japanese communal dancing and live music! Put on your most colourful dance clothes, kimono, or yukata, and join members of the Yoi Yoi collective as they teach you several traditional 'bon dances'. No dance experience is needed—just bring your enthusiasm and be ready to move! The dances will be accompanied by the exhilarating live music of Nagata Shachu, creating an unforgettable atmosphere where everyone can join in. The evening begins with a special 20-minute performance of Japanese folk music by a shamisen ensemble led by Aki Takahashi, setting the stage for an evening of dance, music and celebration. Whether you come to dance, listen, enjoy a drink, or simply soak up the atmosphere, everyone is welcome, at this casual and intimate celebration at Hugh’s Room. With only 130 tickets available per event, space is limited, so get your tickets early and come celebrate with us—Yoi Yoi!

events.title: PINER w/ Emma Worley and Ladybug
events.description: Come out for this folk/alt/rock night as we welcome Piner to the city, celebrate Emma Worley's new album, and enjoy Ladybug's tender tunes!. Piner: a singer-songwriter from Katarokwi (Kingston, ON) whose blend of confessional songwriting, gritty guitar, and tender melodies invites both reflection an…
events.details: Piner: a singer-songwriter from Katarokwi (Kingston, ON) whose blend of confessional songwriting, gritty guitar, and tender melodies invites both reflection and resistance. Piner’s album "A Netherworld", recorded at Joel Plaskett’s studio, is rooted in hope amid challenging times. A Winnipeg Folk Festival Young Performers alumni, Piner has shared bills with Basia Bulat, Mo Kenney, The Crash Test Dummies and more. Her most recent single, “Odelia,” is a powerful pop/rock track rooted in storytelling that confronts gender inequality, inherited expectations, and the radical act of self-trust. / Instagram Emma Worley: on her sophomore album, Forever Beginner, Emma Worley tucks grief, joy, humour, and pain into the same fold. Emerging during a transformative period in her life, the record is an open-hearted, self-reckoning body of work blending alternative folk and Americana. The album was crafted over two years with producer, multi-instrumentalist, and longtime collaborator Ben Whiteley (The Weather Station, Joan Shelley). The arrangements are a textural delight, featuring outstanding players with Worley’s tender voice and poignant songwriting at the centre.

events.details: Following the wildly popular success of his first two Canada-wide tours, “Don’t Lie...You Were Thinking It Too!” and “Nargis’ Son,” Zul Gulamhusein is back with his brand-new third tour, “We Need to Talk”. Expanding beyond Canada and venturing into the U.S., Zul brings his signature storytelling, sharp wit, and unapologetically honest humour to a whole new collection of hilarious observations about life. From navigating the unexpected chaos of parenthood and accepting that he's no longer the thug he once thought he was, to figuring out matrimonial responsibilities, surviving the expectations of an immigrant upbringing, and realizing that getting older comes with more aches, responsibilities, and significantly less patience, nothing is off limits. And, of course, he's still finding creative ways to wish minor inconveniences on people who get on his nerves — because apparently, maturity doesn't mean letting things go. “We Need to Talk” is a hilarious, relatable and brutally honest look at growing up, growing older, and realizing that life didn't exactly turn out the way you planned. One thing's for sure: after this show, you'll have a few things to talk about!

events.title: GLORY! – Opening Night
events.description: a We Quit Theatre production presented by Buddies. January 20 – 24, 2027 $15 – $80 + hst co-created by Emma Beech, Dhanu Chinniah, Arne MacPherson, Gislina Patterson, and Dasha Plett directed by Gislina Patterson A contemporary dance docu-drama. A love letter to our enemies.
events.details: January 20 – 24, 2027 $15 – $80 + hst co-created by Emma Beech, Dhanu Chinniah, Arne MacPherson, Gislina Patterson, and Dasha Plett directed by Gislina Patterson A contemporary dance docu-drama. A love letter to our enemies. A transfeminist fantasia. A bad idea and a good time. Come into the mansion. Nothing bad could possibly happen. Join Shel Silverstein, Gloria Steinum, Hugh Hefner, and various prey animals in the labyrinthine Playboy mansion to explore party planning, 70’s idealism, and the neo-liberal melodrama of the trans scapegoat via popular children’s music. In We Quit Theatre ’s signature mix of delight and iconoclasm, GLORY! mines the political, aesthetic, and libidinal contradictions of the ‘70s to grapple with our present moment of crisis. A foil to second-wave feminism and a deep throated scream for trans aliveness, GLORY! is a party you don’t want to miss. This production is part of the Queer Voices Canada series supported by Canadian Heritage. We Quit Theatre is a performance collaboration between transsexual artists Dasha Plett and Gislina Patterson. events.title: Tafelmusik Voices of the Violin
events.description: Tafelmusik Voices of the Violin Live in the Green Sanderson Hall at Hugh's Room, 296 Broadview Avenue Show at 8pm, Doors at 7pm $40+ in advance, $47+ at the door, $20+ student/arts worker/underemployed ticket Voices of the Violin explores the astonishing range of the unaccompanied violin across more…
events.details: Tafelmusik Voices of the Violin Live in the Green Sanderson Hall at Hugh's Room, 296 Broadview Avenue Show at 8pm, Doors at 7pm $40+ in advance, $47+ at the door, $20+ student/arts worker/underemployed ticket Voices of the Violin explores the astonishing range of the unaccompanied violin across more than three centuries. Performed by Julie Wedman, and stripped of accompaniment, a single instrument becomes many: storyteller, dancer, orator, and virtuoso by turns. The program moves from the concise, improvisatory gestures of 17th- and 18th-century preludes and dances—by Corbett, Purcell, Lonati, Telemann, Vitali, Jacquet de La Guerre, and Vilsmaÿr—to the monumental unaccompanied works of Biber and Bach, before Andrew Balfour carries that same solitary voice into the present day. Across four centuries, the question remains constant: how can four strings speak with so many voices? About Tafelmusik: Every now and then a group of musicians comes along and changes the way we think about music. For over four decades, Tafelmusik has been synonymous worldwide with dynamic, engaging, and soulful performances informed by scholarship, passion and artistic excellence.

events.details: Dave Gunning Live in the Green Sanderson Hall at Hugh's Room, 296 Broadview Avenue Show at 8pm, Doors at 7pm $35+ in advance, $42+ at the door, $18 Student, Underemployed, Arts Worker Tickets With over two decades on the road and fifteen albums to his credit, Nova Scotia’s Dave Gunning has earned a reputation as one of Canada’s most engaging and respected folk singer-songwriters. A multiple East Coast Music Award and Canadian Folk Music Award winner, Gunning is celebrated for his warm stage presence, razor-sharp wit, and songs that honour everyday heroes while tackling hard truths. His music has long reflected his deep roots in Pictou County, where stories of working people, small-town struggles and local pride shape his songwriting. Whether he’s shining a light on unsung community champions or confronting social and environmental issues close to home, Gunning brings an honesty and empathy to his work that have become his trademark. Known for his ability to connect with audiences through both laughter and reflection, Gunning’s live shows balance heartfelt storytelling with moments of perfectly timed humour.

events.description: Join Indigenous artist Marissa Magneson for an immersive workshop where you’ll learn the art of beading to create your own custom hoop earrings. Marissa will guide you through beading techniques and share the cultural significance behind this beautiful craft.
events.details: Join Indigenous artist Marissa Magneson for an immersive workshop where you’ll learn the art of beading to create your own custom hoop earrings. Marissa will guide you through beading techniques and share the cultural significance behind this beautiful craft. This workshop is perfect for those looking to connect with Indigenous art while creating a unique, handmade accessory. Just in time for the holiday season! Recommended for participants 16+. Includes instruction, materials, and access to all current exhibitions . About the Facilitator Marissa Magneson is a Cree-Métis artist, photographer, educator, and workshop facilitator currently pursuing her Ph.D. at York University in the Faculty of Education, where she is researching Beadwork as Pedagogy: A Bridge Towards Cultural Reclamation and (re)Conciliation. She has a BFA honours degree from York University (Toronto, Canada) and a Master’s degree in Canadian and Indigenous Studies from Trent University (Peterborough, Canada). Her research explores Indigenous methodologies using beadwork as visual storytelling. Marissa’s work is rooted in decolonizing education, strengthening community, and cultural reclamation.

events.title: GLORY!
events.description: a We Quit Theatre production presented by Buddies. January 20 – 24, 2027 $15 – $80 + hst co-created by Emma Beech, Dhanu Chinniah, Arne MacPherson, Gislina Patterson, and Dasha Plett directed by Gislina Patterson A contemporary dance docu-drama. A love letter to our enemies.
events.details: January 20 – 24, 2027 $15 – $80 + hst co-created by Emma Beech, Dhanu Chinniah, Arne MacPherson, Gislina Patterson, and Dasha Plett directed by Gislina Patterson A contemporary dance docu-drama. A love letter to our enemies. A transfeminist fantasia. A bad idea and a good time. Come into the mansion. Nothing bad could possibly happen. Join Shel Silverstein, Gloria Steinum, Hugh Hefner, and various prey animals in the labyrinthine Playboy mansion to explore party planning, 70’s idealism, and the neo-liberal melodrama of the trans scapegoat via popular children’s music. In We Quit Theatre ’s signature mix of delight and iconoclasm, GLORY! mines the political, aesthetic, and libidinal contradictions of the ‘70s to grapple with our present moment of crisis. A foil to second-wave feminism and a deep throated scream for trans aliveness, GLORY! is a party you don’t want to miss. This production is part of the Queer Voices Canada series supported by Canadian Heritage. We Quit Theatre is a performance collaboration between transsexual artists Dasha Plett and Gislina Patterson. events.details: Robert Burns: A Passion for Freedom Live in the Green Sanderson Hall at Hugh's Room, 296 Broadview Avenue Show at 8pm, Doors at 7pm $50+ in advance, $57+ at the door Featuring RH Thomson, Beau Dixon, Suba Sankaran, Alina Kuzma, Lucas Harris, D Greenberg and Dylan Bell. On Robbie Burns' birthday (January 25th), the renowned actor RH Thomson and a group of notable Toronto classical, roots and world musicians will celebrate Burns' profound influence on freedom moments around the world. In a 75-minute show devised by Alison Mackay, well known for her special attractions for Tafelmusik, the seven-member ensemble features stories and songs related to American abolitionist Frederick Douglass, India's Nobel Prize-winning poet Rabindranath Tagore and Ukrainian poet laureate Taras Shevchenko, as well as the songs and poetry of Burns himself. events.details: The Two Bobs Live in the Green Sanderson Hall at Hugh's Room, 296 Broadview Avenue Show at 8pm, Doors at 7pm $39+ in advance, $46+ at the door, $30 student, arts worker, and underemployed Bob Dylan and Bob Marley, what did they have in common? Why the first name of course! And a passion for great songwriting! Join us at Hugh’s Room to celebrate two musical icons. On January 29, 2027, Hugh’s Room Live welcomes Fergus Hambleton and Jason Wilson for The Two Bobs: Songs For The World , an inventive celebration of the music of Bob Dylan and Bob Marley. The evening will put a unique spin on the two legendary songwriters’ repertoires: Dylan’s songs reimagined through reggae and ska, and Marley’s through folk and bluegrass. Though they came from very different worlds, Dylan and Marley shared a deep connection to traditional song and used their music to explore love, politics, social change, and the human experience. Featuring Jason Wilson, Fergus Hambleton, Tim Bovaconti , and special guests Jerry Leger and Drew Jurecka , this promises to be an unforgettable evening of songs, stories, and unexpected musical connections. In 1842, in Hamburg, the struggling family of the 9 year-old prodigy Johannes Brahms very nearly moved to the USA so that their genius son could become a touring child sensation. In the antebellum America of minstrel shows, civil war and the constant need for capital, who would this other Brahms have become? He would have escaped the burden of being hailed as the successor to Beethoven at age 20, and spared the trauma of all night dances at Hamburg's harbour brothels when he was just 13, but what would this American Brahms have accomplished, and what would these two versions of the great composer have to say to each other? With Michael Bridge , accordion and Yolanda Bruno, violin.

Their performances have been described as “brilliant” (The Sunday Times, UK), “truly exhilarating” (The WholeNote, Canada), and “absolutely captivating…through a tremendous mastery of their instruments” (Pizzicato Magazine, Luxembourg). ​ Cellist Bryan Cheng , the only prizewinner of both the Queen Elisabeth and Geneva International Music Competitions in 40 years, and pianist Silvie Cheng , former Cecilia Concerts Musician-in-Residence and National Arts Club Artist Fellow, have cultivated a lifelong musical dialogue, forged in childhood and refined through years of shared artistry. Since officially founding the Cheng² Duo with their 2011 Carnegie Weill Recital Hall debut, they have toured extensively across the Americas, Europe, Asia and South Africa.

He continues to evolve as an artist by “doing it his way”, an effort that has been rewarded with an impressive song catalogue and a discerning loyal fan base. Having decided on a career in music during his teens, then setting his sights upon being a guitarist, Alfie Zappacosta would go on to become one of Canada’s most promising and accomplished rock stars. When his vocal dexterity and song writing proficiency were uncovered by a publisher while writing for his first original band Surrender, events would be put in motion to champion Zappacosta (dropping his first name) as a solo artist and bring him to the world’s attention. “Start Again”, “Passion”, “When I Fall in Love Again” and “Nothing Can Stand In Your Way” became staples on Canadian adult contemporary radio and Zappacosta became a personified rock star.

events.details: SEXSMITH SINGS COHEN "All Leonard, No Hallelujah" Live in the Green Sanderson Hall at Hugh's Room, 296 Broadview Avenue Show at 8pm, Doors at 7pm $50+ in advance, $62+ at the door SEXSMITH SINGS COHEN “All Leonard, No Hallelujah” After the success of his Sexsmith Sings Lightfoot and Sexsmith Sings Zevon shows, Ron Sexsmith returns to Hugh’s Room Live on Thursday February 18 for one final tribute show: Sexsmith Sings Cohen: “All Leonard, No Hallelujah.” Ron Sexsmith's songwriting journey began back in 1985 and coincided with his discovery of Leonard’s music and the birth of Ron’s first child. Sexsmith credits Leonard Cohen’s influence as the inspiration for writing his first proper song, “Speaking With The Angel”. As with previous “Sexsmith Sings...” concerts, Ron will perform two solo sets comprised of his favourite Cohen compositions – except for “Hallelujah” which has been done to death. The show will include anecdotes and personal insights into Leonard's songs in what will truly be a full circle moment and an intimate and loving tribute.

Sexsmith credits Leonard Cohen’s influence as the inspiration for writing his first proper song, “Speaking With The Angel”. As with previous “Sexsmith Sings...” concerts, Ron will perform two solo sets comprised of his favourite Cohen compositions – except for “Hallelujah” which has been done to death. The show will include anecdotes and personal insights into Leonard's songs in what will truly be a full circle moment and an intimate and loving tribute.
